newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - January 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - January 16.

text.p: Prepared by The Broadcast Monitoring Company for Reuters
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- HOME OF FORD ESCORT FACES CLOSURE THREAT

Unions are preparing for the closure of Ford's Halewood assembly plant on Merseyside with the loss of up to 1,500 jobs. They expect to be told today that the plant has lost the battle to build a replacement model of the Escort. Ford has indicated that the new model, due out next year, will be built in Germany and Spain.
-- SOUTHAMPTON DIRECTORS NET SHARE BONANZA

All six directors of Southampton football club, including Football Association chairman Keith Wiseman, spent 150 stg each on shares in the club months before its floatation and have seen their value increase to 66,480 stg. The shares were purchased from a mystery shareholder who wanted to sell out of the club. Southampton chairman Guy Askham said the shares were purchased while several offers for possible takeovers were being considered.
-- LANG DISMISSES LEGAL THREAT TO BA ALLIANCE

Trade and industry secretary Ian Lang has dismissed the threat of legal action from the European Commission over the government's possible clearance, without significant changes, of the British Airways and American Airlines alliance. He said that Britain, rather than Brussels, had jurisdiction over the link-up and dismissed the threat from competition commissioner Karel van Miertas a "contribution to the consultive process".
THE TIMES
-- JOBLESS FALL ADDS TO RATE RISE SPECULATION

There is growing speculation within London's financial markets that Chancellor Kenneth Clarke and Governor of the Bank of England, Eddie George, will not agree to another quarter point rise in base rates because of evidence of a disappointing Christmas shopping season and good inflation figures. The City believes that, despite the latest job figures from the Office for National Statistics, the Chancellor will hold out against any Bank of England desire for a rate rise this month.
-- ESSO PAYS 200 MLN STG PRICE FOR WATCHING SUPERSTORES

Esso will continue with its Pricewatch campaign, matching the lowest competing local price at the petrol pump, despite costing the oil company 200 million stg last year. Esso says the campaign was successful in restoring market share lost to discounters, mainly the food superstores, and reclaiming one million customers. But oil consultant Wood Mackenzie said Esso sacrificed a third of its British profits in an effort to match superstore pump prices.
THE GUARDIAN
-- CHRISTMAS CHEER FOR WOOLWORTHS

The overall picture over the Christmas period is of restrained spending, with housing related sales doing well but a mixed performance elsewhere, even within the same sector. Keen prices helped Woolworths record strong Christmas sales but trading reports from three other retailers added to the picture of patchy spending. Kingfisher reported buoyant sales at Comet and Woolworths while Allders said sales had been good before and after Christmas. But the Body Shop did badly, and Laura Ashley did well in Britain but struggled in the United States and continental Europe.
-- CAA TO REQUIRE PERSONAL INDEMNITIES FROM TOUR OPERATORS

A series of company failures during 1996 has led the Civil Aviation Authority to launch a series of measures intended to tighten regulation of licensed sellers of flights and holiday packages. The aim of the regulation is to prevent companies from selling more flights than they are licenced to sell, which the CAA says has become a problem among holders of the Air Travel Organisers Licence. The regulations will come into effect in April.
-- HAMBROS ARM BIDS FOR QUEENS MOAT HOTELS

The principle venture capital arm of Hambros bank, Hambro European Ventures, is preparing to back a 90 million stg buyout of 25 Queens Moat Hotels, put up for sale last April. The deal has been delayed by the death of John Swarbrick, a former Thistle Hotels executive lined up as part of the management team. The bid has prevailed over a similar offer from Adams Hotels, a small Glasgow-based company, which had secured funding from the Royal Bank of Scotland.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- WATER REGULATOR WARNS ONE-OFF PRICE CUTS POSSIBLE

Ian Byatt, industry regulator, has warned MPs at the Commons Trade and Industry Select Committee that privatised water companies could be hit by the kind of one-off price cuts which have driven British Gas to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission. He claims that one-off price cuts are back on the agenda, after being rejected in his last price review in 1994. The principle of the one-off cut has also been used by Stephen Littlechild, electricity regulator, in his price cap for National Grid.
-- PENSION FUND VOICES FEARS OVER MORGAN GRENFELL

Geoff Henry, chief executive of the Merchant Navy Officers' Pension Fund and a top pension fund client of Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM), has indicated that the suspension of one of the City's best known fund managers, Nicola Horlick, could be a decisive factor in prompting him to take his business elsewhere. His group has around 50 million stg invested with MGAM and Henry says the trustees of his fund were concerned about the management structure of the group when the Peter Young scandal was uncovered.
-- BOE APPOINTS BUXTON AS DIRECTOR

Barclays Bank chairman Andrew Buxton is one of the two new directors appointed by the Bank of England, becoming the first serving chairman of a clearing bank to become a member of the court. The deputy chairman of the Bank responsible for the financial structure area, Alastair Clark, will become executive director of that division. They replace Sir Jeremy Morse, formerly a chairman of Lloyds Bank, and Pen Kent, who are both retiring.
